title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority routing, burst controls and utilization reporting enhancement
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Customers using Dedicated capacity reported uneven tail latency and unexpected burst throttling during multi-tenant high-priority workloads. This PR implements priority-aware routing in the dedicated autoscaler, adds tunable burst controls (token-bucket smoothing + short-term burst pool), and improves utilization reporting to surface per-priority and per-fleet metrics. Design: 1) Priority routing: requests carry a priority tag that the autoscaler uses to bias pod placement and scheduling (high/medium/low). We introduce a lightweight priority binning step in the scheduler and a routing policy that prefers nodes with spare capacity for high priority. 2) Burst controls: token-bucket parameters per-priority and a shared burst pool for short spikes; smoothing window configurable via cluster-config and per-fleet overrides. 3) Utilization reporting: new Prometheus labels and metrics (fleet_utilization_total, fleet_utilization_by_priority, burst_pool_usage) plus Grafana dashboard updates. Implementation details: scheduler changes in redwood/serving/autoscaler, token-bucket implementation in redwood/serving/rate_limiter, metrics glue in redwood/observability/metrics, and API surface for fleet config in redwood/private_api. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged when priority is not set. Config keys are opt-in. Testing: unit tests for token-bucket smoothing and priority routing decisions, integration test suite simulating mixed-priority workloads, and end-to-end perf run against a dedicated test cluster. Rollout plan: feature flag off by default; staged rollout to canary fleets for 48h, then gradual ramp to all dedicated fleets if no regressions. Hotfix/rollback: feature flag + quick revert PR available. See related: ENG-4281, PM-302, incident SUP-1123. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Perf benchmarks attached - [x] Docs updated (console + API) - [x] Added dashboards and alert rules

review_thread: Marco: Can we avoid hot loops in the scheduler when priorities flip frequently? Please add a cooldown.

Nina: Burst pool looks good but we should surface a per-customer limit to prevent noisy neighbor. Any plan?

perf_results_summary: Canary perf run: 20% reduction in 99th latency for high-priority requests under mixed workloads, overall throughput unchanged, burst cost increase ~3% for short windows (configurable). Full logs attached in the PR artifacts.
release_notes: Enhanced dedicated autoscaler with priority-aware routing, configurable burst controls, and improved per-priority fleet utilization metrics. Feature gated and disabled by default; enable via fleet config.
